question_text: Read the following text and fill in each gap with a
stimulus: suitable word based on the information of the text.15 = 5 Bhutanese men wear Gho-a knee length robe-and women wear kira- a sheet like cloth piece. Bhutanese houses are built from mud and stone; with wooden shingle roof. The Bhutanese never use iron nails in their buildings. Usually, the Bhutanese build each other's houses by exchanging labour within the community. Different festivals are celebrated all year round in Bhutan. Colourful masks are used in the festivals which reflect the rich Bhutanese culture. Dances are performed by the Buddhist monks to protect the valleys and ward off evil spirits. The main religious festival is called Theseus. The teachings of Lord Buddha are enacted through mask dances for three-five days in the country and of the monasteries people attend these events in their best clothes, with picnic baskets. Another major festival is called Losar. It is celebrated on Lunar New year. People cook special dishes and wear new clothes. It is a time for family get together. Men play archery or darts while women sing and dance. [Unit-6; Lesson-5] The Bhutanese are (a) ⎯ to use iron nalls in making their houses. They (b) ⎯ use mud and stone with wooden shingle roof in their houses. Reciprocal labour is (c) ⎯ in building their houses within their community. Most of the (d) ⎯ are Buddhists. So, during the festivals, the Buddhists monks (e) ⎯ to protect the valleys and ward off evil sprits. Read the passage and answer the questions 4 and 5. Mother Teresa is remembered by the world for her selfless service to the poor and the sick. She was born Yugoslavia on August 27, 1910. Her original name was Agnes Gonxha Bojaxhiu. At the age of twelve, she realized that what she wanted to do most of all was to help the poor. She decided to train for missionary work and came to India at the age of nineteen to join the Sisters of Lorstto, an Irish community of nuns with a mission in Kokkata. In 1928 she took her initial vows as a nun. From 1929 to 1948 Mother Teresa taught at St. Mary's High School in Kolkata, but the suffering and poverty she glimpsed outside the convent walls disturbed her she left the convert school and devoted herself to working among the poor in the slums of Kolkata. She had no money and so she started an open-air school for homeless children. Actually for Mother, life was a mission to serve the suffering humanity. In 1948, Sister Teresa became Mother Teresa. In the same year, she became an Indian citizen. She established the Missionaries of Charity In Kolkata. In 1957, the Missionaries began to work with leprosy is not contagious. She founded Nirmal Hridoy, Shishu Bhavan, Mahatma Gnadhi Leprosy Ashrm and many Organizations. Now the Missionaries of Charity are working in 126 countries with more than 750 centres. Mother Teresa was awarded the Padma Shri and Bharat Ratna. This humanitarian died in 1997.
